comparator.name: Pharmacy
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 programme-specific TER defines a three-year, 180-EC bachelor with two majors. The selected eponymous Major Pharmacy consists of the shared 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year, 45 EC of compulsory third-year Pharmacy study including a 15-EC Bachelor Research Project, and 15 EC of restricted Pharmacy electives. The formal curriculum therefore contains 165 EC of compulsory study and 15 EC of restricted choice, with no free minor space. The bachelor programme page confirms the programme's integrated scientific and professional identity across chemistry, biology, medicine, drug development and manufacture, drug action and safety, pharmaceutical care, patient communication and pharmaceutical research.
components: Medicines Group: Drugs for the Central Nervous System
Medicines Group: Drugs for the Circulatory System
Medicines Group: Drugs for the Endocrine, Digestive and Respiratory System

Three 5-EC Pharmacy electives selected from the official list; retained as restricted-choice space rather than inventing a student choice.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic bachelor Pharmacy. The 2026-2027 TER offers Major Pharmacy and Major Medical Pharmaceutical Sciences. Major Pharmacy is the eponymous route, contains the programme's full compulsory pharmaceutical-care and drug-science sequence, and is the route that directly reflects the target's broad professional and scientific identity. It is therefore selected independently of UCR fit; the alternative MPS major is a research-oriented route with a 30-EC free minor.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease, pharmacology & biomedical research
alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular disease, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, immunity, pathology, epidemiology, laboratory methods and quantitative evidence. This related-fields route addresses how medicines act and how effectiveness and toxicity are evaluated, but it does not provide pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, pharmacokinetics or pharmacy-practice training.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by molecular disease mechanisms, pharmacology, biomedical laboratory work, epidemiology and quantitative research. The label states those supported emphases without presenting the programme as Pharmacy or pharmaceutical chemistry.
progression: Programming, mathematics, statistics, data, life-science, brain-and-behaviour and research foundations precede physiology, biochemistry, molecular-cell biology, laboratory work and advanced pharmacology, pathology, immunity, health psychology and evidence synthesis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned terms pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Medicine use, health behaviour & patient-centred care
alternatives.concept: Study safe and effective medicine use through pharmacology, epidemiology and evidence synthesis, then examine adherence, patient experience, risk communication, behavioural decision-making, health inequalities, ethics and collaborative care. This route addresses the patient-facing and societal side of medicines but does not teach pharmacotherapy, dispensing, clinical pharmacy practice or professional pharmacist communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines epidemiology, pharmacology, health psychology, communication, behavioural decision-making, sociology, ethics and research methods. The label reflects medicine-use and patient-context questions without claiming pharmaceutical-care competence.
progression: Health, brain-and-behaviour, psychology, sociology, leadership and research-method foundations precede statistics, pharmacology, health psychology, persuasive communication, evidence synthesis and behavioural economics. All formal prerequisites and exact planned terms pass; seven courses are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The biomedical route and the patient-centred route share 10 courses and each has 14 different courses / 105 EC. The second route replaces molecular, laboratory, computational and disease-mechanism depth with social psychology, communication, sociology, leadership, rights, AI ethics, lifespan development and behavioural decision-making.

candidates.label: Medicine use, health behaviour & patient-centred care
Drug discovery, pharmaceutical chemistry & formulation
candidates.assessment: UCR has biochemistry and pharmacology but no cumulative chemistry, pharmaceutical analysis, dosage-form technology, biopharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, organic synthesis, drug design or formulation-and-delivery sequence. A third programme would misrepresent general life-science and data courses as pharmaceutical development training.

selection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible: one centred on molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical evidence, and one centred on medicine use, health behaviour and patient context. The next generator-backed direction is drug discovery, chemistry and formulation; UCR cannot implement it, so production stops at two and preserves the specialist and professional gaps explicitly.

blocks: Both directly study human physiology; the external curriculum embeds it in Pharmacy.
Both study molecular-cell structure and processes; the UCR course is not a pharmaceutical sequence.
Both study drug targets and pharmacological mechanisms, while the Groningen sequence is deeper and pharmacy-specific.
Both examine mechanisms of human disease; UCR does not add pharmaceutical treatment training.
Both address immune mechanisms relevant to treatment, but UCR is biomedical rather than immunopharmacological.
Both provide biological laboratory work; UCR lacks pharmaceutical analysis and formulation laboratories.
Both examine population-level health and treatment evidence; UCR does not teach pharmacy-specific utilisation research.

notes.text: Groningen Pharmacy integrates chemistry, biology, medicine, drug development and manufacture, pharmacology, pharmacotherapy, pharmaceutical care and professional formation. UCR can offer coherent related programmes in biomedical drug mechanisms or the behavioural and social dimensions of medicine use, but neither is a Pharmacy degree or route to pharmacist qualification.

UCR has no pharmaceutical-analysis, formulation, biopharmaceutics, pharmacokinetics, medicinal-chemistry, synthesis, drug-group, dispensing or pharmacy-practice sequence. Its pharmacology, life-science, epidemiology, psychology and communication courses remain bounded related contributions rather than substitutes for those components.
